title: Costco facts of the day - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Costco sold 157.4 million rotisserie chickens last year, nearly double a decade ago, holding the price at $4.99 since 2009 as US retail chicken prices roughly doubled, using the bird as a textbook loss leader offset by higher-margin cuts.

insights.claim: Costco has held its rotisserie chicken price at $4.99 since 2009 even as the US retail price of chicken almost doubled, using the product as a textbook loss leader to sustain member loyalty.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A concrete example of deliberate loss-leader pricing that anchors membership retention despite input-cost inflation.
insights.quote: the birds have cost only $4.99 since 2009 even as the US retail price of chicken almost doubled
insights.locator: Roasted in ovens in the rear

insights.claim: Costco sold 157.4 million rotisserie chickens worldwide last year, almost double the volume of a decade ago.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Quantifies the scale of a single loss-leader SKU and its doubling over ten years.
insights.quote: Costco sold 157.4mn rotisserie chickens worldwide last year, almost double the number of a decade ago.

insights.claim: Costco offsets rotisserie losses by processing the same chicken into higher-margin cuts, such as raw breast meat sold at $2.99 a pound, at its Nebraska plant.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Shows the vertically integrated margin structure that makes the $4.99 loss leader sustainable.
insights.quote: Raw breast meat, for example, sells for $2.99 a pound, helping make up for losses on rotisserie.
insights.locator: Rotisserie accounts for only a portion

insights.claim: A retired Costco executive who oversaw the Nebraska site says $4.99 is below what the chicken can be produced for: 'I don’t think you can produce it for that.'
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Insider confirmation that the flagship SKU is priced below cost by design.
insights.quote: It’s $4.99 and for Costco members, that’s one fantastic deal. I don’t think you can produce it for that
